pairs.why: B has the real card's stacked green sheets with white borders and a chunky red X, though its edges are too puffy; A turns it into folded beige paper with a different, papery finish.
B is a clean, readable side view of a properly built locomotive, with the bright, smooth finish of the real bus, while A is a heavy, awkwardly cropped front-angle block.
The two rovers are nearly identical in build, color and finish; A's extra vent detail barely separates them.
A matches the real card's big glass filling the frame and its large, chunky ice cubes, while B is smaller, more photographic and glassier.
A has the real card's soft, puffy scalloped panels and a plain pole with no visible ribs, while B adds exposed rib struts and a stiffer, more mechanical build.
B copies the real color scheme of dark blue number keys and cyan operator keys; A's off-white keys read as a different product.
B matches the real card's green support posts, yellow platform and blue ladder with smooth, clean plastic; A swaps in yellow posts and adds bolted, chunkier slide segments.
B is a wall clock casting a soft shadow on the striped wall, like the real card; A stands on a floor, which changes how it reads.
